description: Rolling-horizon evolutionary planning (RHEA) chooses actions online with a *forward model*: a function that gives the next state and the step cost of an action. At each decision it evolves action sequences of a fixed length (the *horizon*), scores each by rolling it out through the model and summing the step costs (optionally discounted), and then executes only the first action of the best sequence. With *shift buffering*, the next decision starts from the best sequences shifted by one step and padded with a random action, so earlier work is kept. With a population of one, the evolution is random-mutation hill climbing (RMHC); larger populations use elitism, binary tournaments, uniform crossover and point mutation. It spends a fixed number of evaluations per decision and gives no optimality guarantee; use it when you can simulate the system fast, as in real-time games or model-based control.
